styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Diriyah's mud-brick ruins, museums and the old souqs.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Birthplace of the Saudi state at Diriyah and Masmak Fort.

styles.label: Family
styles.blurb: Big malls, indoor parks and desert evenings.

stays.why: Central business district. Walkable to Kingdom Centre, cafés and the metro; easy taxis to most sights.
New financial district with modern hotels and metro links; quiet at night, good for business trips.
Old, budget-friendly heart near Souq Al-Thumairi and Masmak Fort; lively alleys, basic hotels.
Green, calm and embassies; upscale hotels and Wadi Hanifah walks nearby, but you need a car or taxi.

food: Try Saudi staples: kabsa (spiced rice with lamb or chicken), jareesh and kleija sweets.
Al-Bathaa and the old souq area have cheap shawarma, falafel and Indian cafeterias, often under SR 25 a meal.
For a splurge, book a modern Saudi or Levantine restaurant in Olaya or the Diplomatic Quarter; reserve on weekends.
Coffee culture is big: local roasteries serve Arabic coffee (qahwa) with dates; try them at a specialty café.
Alcohol is not sold anywhere. Many restaurants close briefly at prayer times; check opening hours on the day.
more_time: Add a Diriyah evening: the At-Turaif UNESCO site and nearby Bujairi Terrace restaurants are a highlight; check tickets on the day.
Edge of the World: a dramatic cliff viewpoint about 90 minutes' drive out; go with a tour or 4x4, not a normal sedan.
Swap a mall afternoon for Wadi Hanifah or Wadi Namar for a walk and picnic in cooler months.

recommend.why: Two nights cover Diriyah, the old city and a mall or two; add a night for a desert trip or Edge of the World.

month_notes: January: mild days around 21°C, cool nights near 9°C. Best month for walking and Diriyah.
February: pleasant, highs near 23°C. Light jacket for evenings.
March: warming to 28°C, a few rain days. Good for outdoor sights.
April: hot at 33°C by day. Do outdoor sights in the morning.
May: very hot, near 39°C. Stick to malls, museums and evenings.
June: extreme heat, 42°C. Plan indoor days and late nights.
July: hottest month, 43°C. Avoid midday sun entirely.
August: still 43°C. Indoor family activities are the way to go.
September: 40°C, slowly easing. Evenings become bearable late in the month.
October: cooling to 35°C. Outdoor trips get easier.
November: pleasant at 27°C, a couple of rain days. Great for desert trips.
December: mild days near 22°C, chilly nights. Busy holiday season; book ahead.

climate_guide.summary: Hot desert climate: near-constant sunshine, very little rain, and a fierce summer from May to September.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Days around 21–28°C and cool nights. Ideal for Diriyah, the old city and desert trips.

items.title: Summer is extreme (May to September)
items.text: Highs of 39–43°C. Move between air-conditioned places by day; go out after sunset.

items.title: Almost no rain
items.text: At most 2–3 rain days a month in winter and spring. No umbrella needed most trips.

items.title: Nights are cooler but not cool in summer
items.text: Summer lows stay near 26–30°C, so evenings are still hot. Winter nights drop to 9–11°C.

items.title: Pack layers for winter
items.text: December to February evenings are chilly. Bring a jacket and a light layer for strong indoor AC.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, hat and sunscreen; modest clothing for mosques and heritage sites; comfortable shoes for souq alleys.

transit.best: Riyadh Metro for main corridors; taxis or ride apps for everything else.

modes.text: Six lines, about 06:00 to midnight. A 2-hour ticket is SR 4; 3-day pass about SR 20, 7-day SR 40, 30-day SR 140. Tickets include Riyadh Bus.
Riyadh Bus is the main city bus network; fares start around SR 4. Covered by metro passes.
Metered taxis in town usually under SR 30. Uber and Careem work well; many locals agree flat fares of SR 10–15 for short hops.
Driving is the local norm and roads are wide. Check whether your licence needs an International Driving Permit.
Hard in the spread-out north; easy and rewarding in Al-Bathaa's old alleys. Avoid midday heat in summer.
